summary: Nevada County lookout manned since 1911 on a wooden tower; steel tower of 1926 with a 1926 cab; registered 2019 and staffed by volunteers through fire season in 2026.

facts.design: Steel tower with a 1926 Aermotor cab; newspapers give 60 ft (1926, 1971) or 65 ft (1948), replacing a wooden tower of about 40 ft
facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection, Nevada-Yuba-Placer Unit (Cal Fire NEU)

staffing.status: Staffed annually through fire season by volunteer staff

events.note: Wooden lookout tower erected in spring 1911; B.F. Howe began duty July 1, 1911
391 visitors registered at the tower in June
Steel tower built jointly by state and federal forestry departments; register dates the lookout to 1926; newspapers give 60 ft
Three-room observer house completed at the tower base, built by the Forest Service and the state
Station staffed again for a while in October amid debris-burning warnings
Used as a combination fire observation and Ground Observer Corps station (1950s)
Original 1926 Aermotor cab remodeled to add a catwalk
Two students staffed the tower through two fire seasons; a paper boasted of California's first 'Women's Liberation' fire lookout crew
Project description proposes removing trees that obscure the sight-line toward Nevada City, Grass Valley and Cascade Shores
Listed among lookouts that may be staffed during the 2008 fire season
Fire plan says the lookout is staffed annually through fire season by volunteer staff

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1926 as the build date and also says the original platform tower dated from 1911. The 1931 trade report describes a 40-foot frame tower replaced by a 60-foot tower in 1926. The record keeps the 1926 steel tower and adds the 1911 wooden tower as an earlier event.
Newspapers give 60 ft in 1926 and 1971 and 65 ft in 1948. The design line reports both figures and no height_m is given.

notes_for_editor: No source read gives current access or visiting rules, so access is omitted and the story gives no directions. Heights (60 ft in 1926 and 1971, 65 ft in 1948) and the 1911 versus 1926 build dates are unresolved and the story says so. The brief's 1926 build date matches the register field; the 1911 wooden tower is added as an event. The 1926 Livermore and Woodland items and the 1931 Timberman item are read only through the weebly compilation. The register has photo credits (Ron Kemnow, Mark Swift Collection) with no direct image URLs captured, so no photos entry was added. The 2008 CEQA item is a project description, not proof of completion. Confidence is medium because the dates and heights conflict.
